meta.title: Move Chrome Bookmarks to Edge | Snug
meta.description: Move Chrome bookmarks to Edge with Edge's built-in import or an exported HTML file, and when the file is the safer route. Menu paths verified {date}.

title: How do I move my bookmarks from Chrome to Edge?
directAnswer: Open {toImportPath} in Edge. Edge lists these sources: {toImportSources}. Choose Chrome to import directly, or export a file from Chrome with {fromExportPath} and import that. Edge puts imported bookmarks in {toImportPlacement}. Menu paths checked {date}.

builtIn.title: The built-in methods
builtIn.intro: Edge can read Chrome directly, or read a file you export from Chrome. Both are built in.
steps: Direct import: in Edge, open {toImportPath}, choose Chrome as the source and confirm.
With a file: in Chrome, open {fromExportPath}.
With a file: save the file. Chrome names it {fromExportFile}.
With a file: in Edge, open {toImportPath}, choose the HTML file you saved and confirm.

carriesOver.title: What carries over, and when a file is safer
carriesOver.intro: Edge's help lists both sources, so either route works. A file is the safer route when you want a copy to keep before anything changes.
items: Left out of the file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlDrops}.
Where a help page does not say, this page says Not listed instead of guessing.
A file can be opened and checked before you import it, and imported again later. A direct import leaves no file behind.

withSnug.title: With Snug
withSnug.intro: Snug runs in Chrome and Edge, both Chromium browsers. Use it in Chrome to export only the folders you pick, then in Edge to import with a preview.
steps: Install Snug in Chrome and in Edge.
In Chrome, open Snug's Export page and use the checkboxes to select the folders you want, or single bookmarks.
Choose HTML as the format and click Export. Snug downloads the file.
In Edge, open Snug's Import page and choose the file there, or drop it on the page. Do not use the popup for this: it imports at once, without a preview.
The Preview shows the detected format, the bookmark count and the folder tree before anything changes. Bookmarks that Skip duplicates would leave out are marked.

Choose an import mode. Create folder adds everything to a new Imported Bookmarks folder. Restore — merge places bookmarks in their original locations next to your existing ones, when the file carries them.
Leave Skip duplicates on. It leaves out any bookmark whose address is already in Edge, and tells you how many it skipped.
withSnug.snapshot: Create folder and Restore — merge never clear your bookmarks. Before a Restore — replace, Snug saves a Safety snapshot to your Downloads and keeps a copy in Settings, so you can undo the import.

goesWrong.title: If something goes wrong
items: You cannot find the bookmarks after importing. Edge places them in {toImportPlacement}.
Edge does not offer Chrome as a source. Edge lists these sources: {toImportSources}. Use the file route instead.
A bookmark appears twice. Open Duplicates in Snug: it groups copies by address and removes only the copies you mark Delete.
Snug says nothing was imported. Every bookmark in the file is already in your browser. Turn off Skip duplicates to import them again.

verified: Menu paths and file names were read from the official help pages of {fromName} and {toName} on {date}. Browser menus change between versions, so check the source if a path differs on your screen.
